observations.title: Purace volcano (Colombia)
observations.description: The Servicio Geologico Colombiano (SGC) reported intensifying eruptive activity at Puracé during 16-23 September. Signals associated with fluid movement, mainly long-period (LP) events, dominated the seismicity and were located beneath Puracé volcano at depths less than 1 km. Seismic activity associated with rock fracturing (volcano-tectonic earthquakes) continued to be recorded, but a majority of signals were located in an area 13-18 km NE of Puracé at depths of 6-12 km. Sulfur dioxide flux gradually decreased, though it remained above average baseline levels, and soil carbon dioxide concentrations rose throughout the reporting period. Slow ground deformation persisted in an area between the Puracé, Piocollo, and Curiquinga volcanoes. Low-energy thermal anomalies were detected some days on the crater floor. On most days a few ash emissions were detected by the seismic network and/or observed in webcam images. Notably, three ash emissions were detected but not visually observed during 16-17 September and two ash emissions during 20-21 September rose as high as 550 m above the summit. Three ash emissions rose as high as 1.2 km above the summit during 21-22 September and caused ashfall in Cobaló and Coconuco. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Source: Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC)
